newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures end higher in narrow trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures end higher in narrow trade.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended higher Friday, reversing this week's downward trend amid news of maintenance cut next week on the main transmission lines linking the Northwest to southern California,

The 3,800 megawatt (MW) AC segment of the Pacific Intertie was scheduled at 2,950 MW between 0800-1600 PDT Monday to Friday next week, while the DC line will be limited to 2,360 over the same period, Bonneville Power Administration said.
September Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up 34 cents at $30.33 a megawatt hour (MWh) after traded between $30.10 and $30.75.
October PV finished up 35 cents at $23.20. Deferred PV contracts ended five to 60 cents higher.
September California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled up 17 cents at $22.90 after bouncing in 35 cent range.
October COB finished up 10 cents at $22.30. Other COB months ended up 25 to 40 cents.
Firm peak electricity prices for Saturday and Monday at PV were traded at $26.00-27.50 a MWh, while those at COB were sold at $17.50-19.00.
Despite today's modest gains, market sources said the complex will remain rangebound Monday due to the lack of fresh fundamental news.
"We're stuck in a range here. There's really no news to move the market," a West Coast trader said.
Next week, the southern portion of the Southwest was expected to see above normal temperatures, while Colorado and coastal areas were forecast to see seasonal readings.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to average below normal in eastern areas and above normal along the coast.
Most baseload units in the West were said to be operating normally early Friday.
The 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Palo Verde generating complex in Arizona continued to coast down toward its refueling outage in September.
The unit, in Wintersburg, Ariz., was operating at 83 percent power early Friday, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said in its daily plant status report.
